subject.title: Same-chat serial queue: 300s release lets a follow-up turn run while the original task is still running — no write lease, confusing UX on follow-up questions

question: Should a released same-chat turn remain visible and control follow-up semantics through a generic core background-task contract, while resource-specific write serialization stays in the owning tool plugin?
rationale: The issue combines generic session scheduling with a Feishu-specific document mutation concern; choosing one layer without maintainer intent risks a cross-boundary lock or a channel-specific policy that does not generalize.

options.title: Define a generic post-release contract
options.body: Specify status, cancellation, and follow-up behavior for released turns in the generic session scheduler, then implement Feishu document serialization separately.

options.title: Limit the fix to Feishu documents
options.body: Add per-document serialization and outcome handling in the Feishu tool while retaining the current generic queue-release semantics.

options.title: Preserve strict same-chat serialization
options.body: Do not release a same-chat turn while it is active, accepting longer follow-up latency in exchange for one-turn-at-a-time semantics.

recommendation.title: Define a generic post-release contract
recommendation.body: Specify status, cancellation, and follow-up behavior for released turns in the generic session scheduler, then implement Feishu document serialization separately.

likelyOwner.reason: Their adjacent document-write work makes them the strongest available routing candidate for the Feishu half; generic scheduler ownership still needs confirmation.
